extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: This policy outlines Humana's billing requirements for modifier 50 and reimbursement for services reported with modifier 50.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. The following policy applies to professional services only.

extracted_content.title: Billing
extracted_content.content: Bilateral procedures are procedures that are performed on similar sites on opposite sides of the body, during the same session, by the same qualified health care practitioner. When a procedure reported using a service code with a Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS) Relative Value File (RVF) bilateral indicator 1 is performed bilaterally, providers must report the code with either modifier 50 or with anatomical modifiers such as modifiers LT and RT. Humana strongly encourages providers to report a bilateral procedure using modifier 50 rather than modifiers LT and RT, but accepts both methods. When using modifier 50 to report a bilateral procedure, report a single claim line with a unit of 1. When using modifiers LT and RT to report a bilateral procedure, report two claim lines, each with a unit of 1. Only report modifier 50 when the procedure is performed on similar but opposite sites. For example, report modifier 50 for the same service code for a procedure performed on the right and left knee. However, do not report modifier 50 for the same service code for a procedure performed on the right knee and left shoulder. When reporting two or more bilateral procedures using the same code, report the first bilateral procedure on a single claim line with a unit of 1 using modifier 50 and report a single claim line with a unit of 1 for all subsequent bilateral procedures using modifier 50 and modifier 59. It is not necessary to report modifier 50 with a service code with an MPFS RVF bilateral indicator other than 1. Special considerations for billing modifier 50 with certain anatomical modifiers Report modifier 50 in addition to eyelid, finger and toe modifiers on one claim line with a unit of 1 for procedures performed bilaterally on similar but opposite sites. Examples that are considered bilateral and should be billed with the appropriate anatomical modifiers and modifier 50:

extracted_content.content: Upper left eyelid and upper right eyelid: Report modifiers E1 and E3 with modifier 50

extracted_content.title: Billing
extracted_content.content: Left hand, third digit and right hand, third digit: Report modifiers F2 and F7 with modifier 50

extracted_content.title: Billing
extracted_content.content: Left foot, great toe and right foot, great toe: Report modifiers TA and T5 with modifier 50 Examples that are not considered bilateral and should be billed as two claim lines, each with a unit of 1, with the appropriate anatomical modifiers but not with modifier 50:

extracted_content.content: Upper left eyelid and lower right eyelid: Report modifiers E1 and E4

extracted_content.title: Billing
extracted_content.content: Left hand, third digit and right hand, fourth digit: Report modifiers F2 and F8

extracted_content.title: Billing
extracted_content.content: Left foot, great toe and right foot, third digit: Report modifiers TA and T7

extracted_content.content: Humana only applies a bilateral payment adjustment to procedures reported using a service code with a MPFS RVF bilateral indicator 1. When a bilateral payment adjustment applies, the amount allowed for a bilaterally performed procedure is the lesser of the following:

extracted_content.content: A single claim line with an MPFS RVF bilateral indicator 1 code billed with modifier 50 is processed as one unit. Providers may submit supporting documentation for reconsideration of additional units. In certain circumstances, additional payment rules may apply. For example, when a bilaterally performed procedure is reported with another procedure for the same date of service, a multiple procedure payment reduction may be applied after the bilateral payment adjustment. In such cases, the bilaterally performed procedure is considered one unit.

definitions.title: Definitions
definitions.content:
Base maximum amount payable under the member's plan: The maximum amount of reimbursement for a covered expense, determined by the member's plan. Depending on the plan, this may be the maximum allowable fee, the appropriate Medicare fee schedule rate or an amount derived from another payment model. Actual plan reimbursement may be less than this base maximum amount, because of applicable adjustments.

Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS) Relative Value File (RVF): A file published by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) that includes, among other information, bilateral indicator, relative value units and conversion factors for physician services.

Modifier 50: Bilateral procedure.

Modifier 59: Distinct procedural service.

Modifier LT: Left side (used to identify procedures performed on the left side of the body).

Modifier RT: Right side (used to identify procedures performed on the right side of the body).
